name: Nakamura lock
summary: A blunt-nosed glider with a small fold that locks the nose together. Slow, steady and long.

steps.title: Crease the middle
steps.text: Fold the sheet in half the long way, crease it, and open it flat again.

steps.title: Fold the top corners in
steps.text: Bring each top corner down to the center crease.

steps.title: Fold the point down
steps.text: Fold the point down over the flaps so its tip sits about 2.5 cm (1 in) above the bottom edge.

steps.title: Fold the new corners in
steps.text: Bring the two new top corners to the center crease. The tip of the point should still show below them.

steps.title: Lock the flaps
steps.text: Fold the small triangle up over the two flaps. This is the lock that holds the nose together.

steps.title: Turn it over
steps.text: Flip the paper so the folds face down.

steps.title: Fold in half
steps.text: Fold it in half along the center crease. The folds end up on the outside.

steps.title: Fold the first wing
steps.text: Fold the top layer down about 2.5 cm (1 in) from the bottom fold, parallel to it.

steps.title: Turn it over
steps.text: Flip the plane so the other side faces up.

steps.title: Fold the second wing
steps.text: Same fold on this side: about 2.5 cm from the bottom fold, parallel to it.

steps.title: Open the wings
steps.text: Lift both wings until they're level, angled slightly up.

done.title: Ready to glide
done.text: Hold it under the wings and give it a level, gentle push. It glides best indoors or on a calm day.
